stumbles.quote: `query` is the line number of the query in `QUERY_FILE`.
stumbles.why: It doesn't say whether line numbers start at 0 or 1. The example shows `"query": 1`, but that doesn't settle it.

stumbles.quote: every search rescores its top 100 candidates against the float vectors
stumbles.why: It's unclear whether the 100 candidates are fixed or depend on `-k`. It also doesn't say what happens if `-k` is greater than 100.

stumbles.quote: remex skips rescoring and returns the quantized scores.
stumbles.why: It doesn't say what scale the quantized scores are on, or whether they can be compared with rescored scores. The docs also don't say what `--keep-float` does at build time, because the build command isn't shown.

stumbles.quote: `--bits` sets the quantization width used for the search.
stumbles.why: It doesn't say whether this must match or be no larger than the bit width used when the index was built. It also doesn't say which values are valid. Only 2 and 4 appear.

point: `remex search` takes an index and a file of comma-separated query vectors, returns the top `-k` ids and scores per query as JSON Lines, and lets you trade recall for speed with `--bits` and optional float rescoring.
